title: I Tried Faceless YouTube for 3 Years: Here's the Reality
summary: Operator of several faceless channels on the reality: possible but improbable, course methods violate platform rules, costs outrun early revenue, and platform rules change without notice.

assertions.quote: While that certainly is possible, it is quite honestly improbable.

verdicts.note: Partner-program thresholds and typical CPMs mean most channels never reach that; a few outliers do.

assertions.quote: anytime someone is trying to convince you that something is easy, they're probably just trying to sell you something
You get monetized by buying subscribers through a variety of websites.

verdicts.note: Buying subscribers and watch time breaches partner-program rules and triggers removal.

assertions.quote: YouTube is no longer a platform for originality. YouTube is the platform for copy and paste.

verdicts.note: Derivative formats do spread, but duplicative and mass-produced AI content is now explicitly demonetized.

assertions.quote: you can quickly run out of money trying to find the level of success

verdicts.note: Per-video costs with no revenue for months is the standard failure mode; abandoned channels are visible everywhere.

assertions.quote: the people that are are selling those shovels are usually going to be more profitable than the people that are are doing the digging
Don't just rely on a platform that can give and take whenever it feels like it

verdicts.note: Repeated policy changes and mass demonetizations are documented; diversification is standard advice.

assertions.quote: they always tell you about the other niches, but they never they never tell you about their niches at work

verdicts.note: Plausible incentive but no evidence beyond anecdote.
